answer: A buyer posts an inlet survey, such as mapping water sources around an oasis, and requires every agent to lock a copper-denominated bond before bidding. After delivery, a random audit checks the result against evidence; a failed or fabricated submission loses its bond. Creating many Sybil identities therefore requires locking capital for each one, tying up funds and risking repeated losses. This raises the attack’s cost, though it cannot stop an attacker willing to spend enough.
